references.text: The context for this assembly: the entire congregation of Israel gathered as one man to decide what should be done about Gibea ([ref:Judg 20:1-2|Judges 20:1-2]).
The background for the mobilization: the Levite's call to all Israel to take a stand against the shameful act that had been committed ([ref:Judg 19:29-30|Judges 19:29-30]).
The Levite describes the shameful act (נְבָלָה) committed in Gibea and urges the men of Israel to take a stand on the matter ([ref:Judg 20:6-7|Judges 20:6-7]).

A similar logistical system for supplying a large army, where some were selected to gather provisions, was used when Joshua prepared the people to cross the Jordan ([ref:Josh 9:11-12|Joshua 9:11-12]).
Benjamin's response to Israel's mobilization: they refused to hand over the wicked men and gathered for battle against the rest of Israel ([ref:Judg 20:14-15|Judges 20:14-15]).
The term נְבָלָה (shameful deed) used to describe a gross sexual crime in Israel, parallel to Shechem's disgraceful act against Dinah ([ref:Gen 34:7|Genesis 34:7]).
The word נְבָלָה is also used regarding Achan's sin, which was called a shameful deed in Israel ([ref:Josh 7:15|Joshua 7:15]).
Amnon's rape of Tamar is also described with the word נְבָלָה – a shameful deed in Israel ([ref:2 Sam 13:12-13|2 Samuel 13:12-13]).
A similar system for selecting soldiers: one thousand from each tribe was sent out to war against the Midianites ([ref:Num 31:3-4|Numbers 31:3-4]).
